article.name: ELIOT Memory OS
article.summary: ELIOT Memory OS currently publishes a V3 design baseline for a local-first memory daemon, provenance-aware revisions, scoped retrieval, and controlled erasure. Upstream says V3 is not a released runtime and its Store candidate is unqualified; this review reports design contracts, not verified behavior or benchmark results.

who_what.text: The official README describes ELIOT as a local-first memory system that preserves observations, reconstructs current work, supplies context, and learns from outcomes. It explicitly labels the V3 documentation baseline as not a released runtime, so this review treats current V3 behavior as design intent.

architecture.text: V3 assigns observations, revisions, retrieval, context, outcomes, and finite jobs to a Memory daemon; a narrow relay handles host events and context emission, while a private SurrealDB Store is the selected persistence target. The six-table schema and immutable blobs are design selections, not a running or qualified Store.

The model distinguishes accepted observations, interpreted claims, and versioned memories. It specifies exact accepted source bytes/blob references, occurrence and work binding, capture limitations, source relations, revision hashes, and grounds; exact opens are intended to return the requested source or revision without falling forward.

behavior.text: Capture is designed around an immutable bounded command staged before Store send, followed by one transaction that records the observation and relations. Stable native event identity supports deduplication; otherwise retries preserve the original command identity and read back its result. These operations are specified but not qualified in a connected runtime.

Direct corrections use the expected current revision, preserve history, and publish the new revision, source, grounds, replacement, and attributed cause together. Exact retries resolve to the original result; stale revision requests conflict. This is a documented contract, not an observed runtime result.

The design separates withdrawal from erasure. Durable notices are intended to prevent reactivation through stale replay or backup restore; erasure denies reads and requires verified cleanup of controlled Store, blob, spool, and derived copies. A committed notice is not deletion proof. Delivered host transcripts and provider copies remain outside the guarantee, and cleanup implementation/qualification remain open.

Retrieval first resolves addressed work and then unions bounded candidates from direct handles, exact cues, lexical search, optional vectors, grounds/relations, and methods. Scope is applied before candidate limits. Results are intended to expose examined scope, partial/unavailable arms, gaps, and exact source handles; a zero top-K result does not prove global absence.

Scope is designed around project and workspace plus an actual task, or an actual actor/session pair when no task is supplied. The docs reject widening a failed task lookup into a broader substitute. These are design rules, not an authorization or runtime isolation result; upstream disclaims a hostile same-user sandbox.

Provenance rules keep source, representation, and claim identities separate and use exact observation/revision handles, hashes, typed relations, and grounds. Similarity does not establish truth or applicability; unknown support is intended to remain qualified or trigger abstention. No connected V3 provenance path was verified.

Bounded candidate arms, byte caps, deterministic selection, and a bounded lexical snapshot are proposed efficiency controls. Exact token limits require an actual counter; configured limits are not measured usage. Durable readback/status is specified for recovery and cleanup, but no latency, token, cost, storage, or throughput data was collected.

metrics.evidence: V3 specifies bounded retrieval, source handles, and explicit gaps, but no responses were produced or scored.
Expected-revision correction and history are specified, but no correction sequence or stale-value probes were run.
Notice and controlled-copy cleanup contracts were inspected, but no erase operation or post-erase probe was run.
Project/work scoping is specified but no cross-scope workload or authorization audit was run.
Grounds and exact source handles are design contracts; no outputs were adjudicated for evidence support or citation coverage.
No runtime timing samples were collected.
The docs specify bounds but no usage, charge, or storage measurements were collected.

limits.text: This is a bounded review of official V3 documentation at the verified main head. The README says V3 is not a released runtime, V1/V2 are donors, and the Store guide calls its source candidate unmerged and not a working Store. No donor implementation was treated as current V3 evidence.

The registry leaves Store connection/readback, source implementation, runtime qualification, and several cleanup/scenario paths open. The Memory inference extension is also unavailable. These gaps prevent claims of operating correctness or measured performance.

The design does not claim a hostile same-user sandbox, portable encrypted backup, physical media sanitization, deletion from delivered host/provider copies, or demonstrated deployed isolation. Retrieval quality, complete erasure, and performance remain unknown.

benchmark.note: No ELIOT Memory OS runtime, tests, or benchmarks were run. Design contracts and project metric definitions are not system measurements.
